facts.claim: Tornado's XSRF cookie name must be kept in sync between backend config and frontend cookie-read logic, and renaming it fixes stale-cookie auth failures.
facts.evidence: Set `xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf"` in the web `Application` settings ... Updated token lookup in `fetchApi` to read `_mitmproxy_xsrf` instead of `_xsrf` before sending `X-XSRFToken`.

facts.claim: Changing a cookie name that overlaps with browser-default/legacy cookie names (like `_xsrf`) is a reusable fix pattern for stale-state auth bugs, since isolating the app's cookie namespace avoids collisions with previously-set cookies.
facts.evidence: Users with a stale HttpOnly `_xsrf` cookie could no longer update options in mitmweb (`X-XSRFToken: undefined` → 403) ... This change isolates mitmweb from legacy cookie state by migrating XSRF handling to a namespaced cookie name.

facts.claim: Reviewers pushed back on scope creep (added test assertions, unrelated test file changes, committing a verification screenshot) and the fix was narrowed to only the backend/frontend cookie-naming change, with verification shared out-of-repo via PR comments.
facts.evidence: Reverted the added assertion in `test/mitmproxy/tools/web/test_app.py`. Reverted all changes in `web/src/js/__tests__/utilsSpec.tsx`. Kept the production fix focused to backend/frontend cookie naming only. Retested the affected backend/frontend test targets and posted the verification screenshot directly in PR comments (without adding it to the repository).

json.reason: The PR fixes a stale-cookie XSRF bug by renaming the cookie, requiring synchronized backend/frontend changes (F1), establishes a reusable namespacing pattern for avoiding legacy cookie collisions (F2), and the merged history shows reviewers trimmed the PR back to a minimal, focused diff after initial scope creep in tests and artifacts (F3). These are concrete, durable lessons tied to specific mechanisms rather than generic style or narration.
